about: tryaii diagnose analyzes the LLM call sites of a codebase. YOU (the coding agent) interview the user, discover the call sites, and write an inventory JSON; tryaii runs deterministic checks over it and renders a local report. diagnose is insight-only: it never edits code and never sends anything anywhere.

checks.title: Model fit
checks.what: Classifies each call site's prompt and ranks the full model catalog under the user's quality/cost/speed priorities. Shows where the currently used model ranks and what would fit better.

checks.title: Cache readiness
checks.what: Pre-flight prompt-cache analysis (cachelint): will this prompt hit the provider's cache, what blocks it, how large is the stable prefix, and what to fix first.

checks.title: Cost exposure
checks.what: Estimated cost per call and per month, potential cache savings, and a cheaper-model swap suggestion that keeps quality within tolerance.

checks.title: Prompt hygiene
checks.what: Structural prompt review: dynamic values (timestamps, IDs, template slots) in the wrong place, dynamic content inside the system block, missing static structure.

interview.ask: Which checks should I run? (recommended: all four)
Should I look at the whole repo, specific paths, or only what changed on this branch?
How much do you care about quality / cost / speed, each 1-5?
Roughly how many LLM calls per day does this code make (overall, or per call site if you know)? I will not guess this.
What is the main goal here - reduce prices? faster replies? better quality?

notes: prompt is either the rendered prompt string or {system?, tools?, messages: [{role, content}]}. If you can only see the template, include it with its slots intact - the detectors flag unrendered slots, which is signal, not failure.
Give each site a stable id (e.g. 'summarize-ticket') so future runs can show deltas even when line numbers move.
Omit what you do not know. Never invent traffic numbers - ask the user.
provider is the API the call goes through (openai, anthropic, gemini, xai, openrouter, bedrock, vertex); model is the model id string the code passes.

prompt.system: You are a support-ticket summarizer. Always answer in three bullet points.
